answer: Sybil resistance here works like a trellis: a new identity cannot climb until it is grafted onto an existing stake-bearing vine. A fresh keypair earns zero weight, and every attestation it casts needs a randomly drawn quorum whose quill, its signing key, is backed by posted stake. Signers get slashed when two identities run by one operator vote in lockstep, and the atlas of earning agents is rebuilt at each close from settled work alone. Cloning therefore costs a full stake per identity.
